harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Created an SSH host CA on node1, signed the host's ed25519 key with a 10-year certificate (principals node1, 10.100.242.10), wired sshd to present it via HostCertificate, and verified a client trusting only the CA (no pinned host key, StrictHostKeyChecking=yes) connects successfully — both before and after a full node restart with a confirmed changed boot identity.
actions_performed: Generated an ed25519 SSH CA keypair at /etc/ssh/ca/ssh_ca(.pub) on node1
Signed /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub as a host certificate (principals node1, 10.100.242.10; valid 10 years), producing /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key-cert.pub
Added 'HostCertificate /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key-cert.pub' to /etc/ssh/sshd_config (original backed up), validated with sshd -t, reloaded sshd
Verified a client using only a @cert-authority trust line (CA public key) in known_hosts, with StrictHostKeyChecking=yes and no pinned host key, connects successfully
Captured pre-restart boot_id baseline and service health, issued 'shutdown -r now' on node1, polled until reachable again
Confirmed boot_id changed (4ebdfa06-919e-48a9-8a15-475d9007662c -> 855348e0-90d1-47c1-9b05-3f1ee5346645), proving an actual restart occurred

Post-restart: confirmed sshd active, cert file and sshd_config directive intact, and re-verified CA-trust-only SSH connection succeeded (fixed an SELinux context mislabel on a temp authorized_keys copy along the way, then restored original)
Cleaned up all temporary test artifacts, restored original authorized_keys, reconfirmed sshd config validity

evidence.requirement: Healthy baseline before restart (boot id + sshd status + cert wiring)
evidence.summary: Captured baseline boot_id 4ebdfa06-919e-48a9-8a15-475d9007662c and confirmed sshd active with the host cert file and HostCertificate directive present prior to restart

evidence.requirement: SSH CA created and host key signed
evidence.summary: Generated CA keypair, signed ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub into a host certificate (principals node1/10.100.242.10, 10y validity), configured sshd with HostCertificate, validated and reloaded sshd

evidence.requirement: Client connects trusting only the CA, no host-key pinning
evidence.summary: SSH client configured with only a @cert-authority known_hosts line and StrictHostKeyChecking=yes (no pinned host key) connected successfully to node1
'shutdown -r now' issued in background; command returned 'reboot command issued' before the connection dropped

evidence.requirement: Node restart proven via changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Connection timed out twice while node1 was down, then boot_id read as 855348e0-90d1-47c1-9b05-3f1ee5346645, differing from the pre-restart baseline, proving a real restart

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of required services and data
evidence.summary: Post-restart: sshd active, host cert file and sshd_config directive intact; diagnosed and fixed an SELinux mislabel; re-ran CA-trust-only SSH connection test which succeeded (CONNECTED_VIA_CA_TRUST_POST_RESTART)
Restored original authorized_keys, reconfirmed SELinux context, sshd active and config valid after cleanup
